solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ape, primate one's shot

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or worn out, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a monkey's attempt at something has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a noun beside 'primate', but it is a verb and the definition; 'shot' rearranges PRIMATE ONES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy their manner, which is mimicry of another person.

clue.text: Unbecoming, if daring criminal

indicators.note: a criminal version of the words is a corrupted one, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bold crime is beneath a respectable person's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: INFRA DIG, short for Latin 'infra dignitatem', means beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbecoming is unseemly, lowering one's standing, the very sense of the Latin phrase.

clue.text: Pudding choice no good

parts.note: a plum job or role is a choice one, the best going
duff is British slang for useless or broken

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the selected dessert is poor.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUM DUFF is a British boiled suet pudding with raisins.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled suet dessert with dried fruit, a traditional British example of the category.

clue.text: Sound cheerful once opener's dismissed

indicators.note: with the first letter sent away, like a cricket opening batsman out, the word loses its head

parts.note: a bright mood is a cheerful one

explanation.surface: A cricket team sounds upbeat until its opening batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' is an adjective (sound reasoning), not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is correct, valid and justified, as is one that is on the money.

clue.text: Most of rhyme written in honour of counterpart

indicators.note: the shortened verse is put inside the honour, as if inscribed in it

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, its final letter lost

parts.note: a rhyme or poem is a verse

explanation.surface: Part of a poem composed as a tribute to someone's opposite number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final E of the rhyme word; 'written in' sets the remainder inside the British honour. 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the corresponding opposite side of a coin or argument, its complement.

clue.text: Russian-born writer, name appearing in Scottish town also

indicators.note: the abbreviation turns up inside the town's name

parts.note: Ayr is a town on Scotland's west coast
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A novelist's name crops up in a Scottish town as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Atlas Shrugged was born in St Petersburg before emigrating to America.

clue.text: Put down volunteers in harbour

parts.note: to enter details is to put them down in writing
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers being landed at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' is a verb, as in harbouring doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a thought or hope is to hold and consider it in the mind.

clue.text: Some Anna's hummingbirds in a tree

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are taken, a run spanning the words

explanation.surface: Birdwatching: a few hummingbirds of one species perch up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna's hummingbird is a real North American species.
explanation.definitionFit: A common deciduous woodland species with pinnate leaves and winged keys.

clue.text: Shrewd, like ancient king, leader in Egypt

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
Tut, short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: Someone clever, resembling a pharaoh who once led Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone sharp and canny who judges situations well.

clue.text: German chap getting round Mainz, initially in a cab

parts.note: Hans is a common German man's name
O is round in shape

indicators.note: just the first letter of the city's name is used

explanation.surface: A German man takes a taxi tour around Mainz.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, the original London taxi.

clue.text: Cast following breather

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a lung is the organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: A theatre cast that comes after a rest break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' is the past tense of throw, not actors; 'breather' is not a pause but an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past forms of verbs for throwing or hurling something.

clue.text: One after a score at Monte Carlo?

definitions.text: One after a score at Monte Carlo?

parts.words: One after a score at Monte Carlo?
parts.note: one more than twenty, said in French as spoken in Monaco, is also a casino card game

explanation.surface: A gambler's next bet once points are on the board in Monaco's casino.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so one after it is twenty-one, said in French; it is also the card game known as pontoon or blackjack, fitting the casino.
explanation.definitionFit: The French number twenty-one, also the name of the casino card game played to that total.

clue.text: Check on old character backing theatres

parts.note: an audit is a check of accounts

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

parts.note: an air is a manner or character, as in an air of mystery

explanation.surface: An inspection of an old personality who supports theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoriums are the halls of playhouses where audiences sit; the Latin plural is used.

clue.text: Proportion, or portion, reduced

indicators.note: the word is cut down by one letter, its last

parts.note: a ration is an allotted portion

explanation.surface: A dieter's choice: shrink the proportion or the helping itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, one against another.

clue.text: Operative damaged conifer

indicators.note: a damaged thing is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker has harmed a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operative' looks like a noun (a worker) but is the adjective meaning currently valid.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or rule that is operative is currently valid and has effect.

clue.text: Looking about

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests glancing around, but it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gazing at something and, as a preposition, on the subject of.

clue.text: Expensive organ used by daughter

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A daughter takes up a costly musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' sounds musical but is a body part; 'used by' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dear costs a lot, a British sense of the word.

clue.text: Government supporter, Cavalier having changed sides

indicators.note: right is swapped for left: R becomes L

parts.note: the Cavaliers were the royalists of the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A Civil War Cavalier who has defected to the other faction.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L are abbreviations for right and left, so changing sides swaps one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyalist backs the established authority, staying faithful to the ruling power.

clue.text: Song composed about a duke

indicators.note: the calm word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a composed person is calm, serene

explanation.surface: A piece of music written about an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suggests writing music but means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song sung or played beneath a window at night.

clue.text: On the edge of one's seat since start of Gaslight

definitions.text: On the edge of one's seat

parts.note: ago and since both mark time past (a week ago, a week since)

indicators.note: the opening letter of the film title is taken

explanation.surface: An audience has been gripped since the thriller Gaslight began.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe being eager and excited, keenly waiting to see what happens.

clue.text: Appropriate composer, English

parts.note: Edward German was an English composer of light opera

explanation.surface: A suitable English composer for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is the adjective (fitting), not the verb to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant to the matter in hand, fitting the context.

clue.text: Swindler swindled? Turn a blind eye

parts.note: a con is a swindle, or a con man
done means cheated, as in I've been done

explanation.surface: A con artist gets conned, and the victim chooses to overlook it.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for swindler is short for con man; DONE is British slang for cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or tacitly accept wrongdoing, letting it pass.

clue.text: Army officer is able to, throwing in a tip, liberal

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside the verb

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: a liberal version is a free one, so the letters are loosely rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer can be a generous tipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' looks like a political label but signals the shuffle of 'a tip'; 'throwing in' places those shuffled letters inside the verb for 'is able to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army, above lieutenant and below major.

clue.text: Not quite daring to drink litre

indicators.note: the bold word takes the abbreviation inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: hardy can mean bold or daring

explanation.surface: Someone not quite bold enough to down a litre.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly and barely both mean only just, almost not at all.

clue.text: Two OT characters' collection of odds and ends

parts.note: Job is an Old Testament figure
Lot, Abraham's nephew, is another

explanation.surface: Biblical figures owning assorted bric-a-brac.
explanation.walkthrough: OT is the Old Testament; 'characters' looks like letters but means people.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed bundle of items sold together at auction.

clue.text: Love affair, a rum do, au pair finishes

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the four following words is taken

explanation.surface: A romance with the nanny is a strange business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rum do' is British for an odd affair; 'au pair' is a live-in foreign helper. 'finishes' takes M, O, U, R from rum, do, au, pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love is used in English for a romance, often a secret one.

clue.text: Rogue in favour of cutting repayment

indicators.note: the shorter word cuts into the longer one

parts.note: a rebate is a partial repayment
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone supports slashing refunds.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, a rascal.

clue.text: Love game, unfortunately — last of a series

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the word ends up in an unlucky muddle, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A tennis loss: a love game, sadly the final one in a run of matches.
explanation.walkthrough: Love game is a tennis term for a game won without the loser scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the end of any sequence.

clue.text: Trouble between a mother and son over spiritual head

indicators.note: the trouble sits in the middle, separating the other pieces
the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy or son
ma is an informal word for mother
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Family strife between a mother and son about a religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the boy round to read backwards at the front; 'between' then slots the trouble in after it, before 'a mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan Buddhist leader is the foremost figure of that faith.

clue.text: Musical — girl is full of it

indicators.note: the name holds the small word inside it

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Showbiz gossip: a vain girl, very pleased with herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of it' suggests boastfulness, but here a girl's name literally contains IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Peron, a well-known theatre production.

clue.text: Still by jetty? Nothing odd in that

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are dropped, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: Is someone waiting quietly by a pier? Nothing strange there.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet and still are synonyms meaning up to now or even so.

clue.text: New cover for one in a series of espionage novels

definitions.text: one in a series of espionage novels

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
a mantle is a cloak or covering

explanation.surface: A spy book in a long series gets a fresh jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenmantle is John Buchan's 1916 Richard Hannay thriller, sequel to The Thirty-Nine Steps.
explanation.definitionFit: This Buchan thriller is the second of the Richard Hannay spy stories.
